mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their previous 12-month averages signals a monetary tightening accompanied by rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly increase in both personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) above 0.4% for two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both rise > 0.4% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the unemployment rate below 0.1 percentage points for six consecutive months, despite steady or rising GDP growth (proxied by GDPC1), signals structural labor market slack that does not translate into demand pressure, resulting in flat or negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE changes in [-0.1, 0.1)% for 6 consecutive months and GDPC1 grows > 0%
regime_hint: structural labor slack with GDP growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative or flat (< +0.2%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals weakening residential investment, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
